question: If John Smith deliberately shares client data with outsiders, can TechCorp terminate him straight away without giving notice?
why: Cited Clause 8 (Confidentiality) for the right to terminate immediately for willful breach of confidentiality; that right is in Clause 7 (Termination), and clause 8's text was not even in the context the answer was generated from. Naming clause 8 as where confidentiality is defined is fine; resting the termination right on it is the bug.
complaint: a lawyer said it cited the wrong clause on termination, maybe Thursday.
logged_answer: Yes. Deliberately sharing client data with outsiders would be a willful breach of confidentiality, which is one of the grounds on which the Company may terminate immediately and without notice. (Clause 8 (Confidentiality))
